answer: A concrete sybil defense: every identity maintains a public mirror of recent work that independent peers audit on demand. The network checks a consistency signal across time; a clone farm fails when its mirrors disagree. The tundra test groups identities by network vantage point and caps each group's voting weight, so a thousand clones behind one uplink count as one voice. An attacker must run a distinct, auditable mirror per identity across many epochs, paying real compute and bandwidth for each while capped reward stays flat.
